data.summary: The current source does not satisfy the assigned navigation non-interference requirement: its fallback explicitly invokes the production keyboardCondition callback during passive inspection and then presses the arrow regardless of the computed eligibility. Observation chronology also contains a synthetic not-ready occurrence ranked immediately after the retained recorder error rather than at its actual detection site. Evidence exposure preserves several inspected repairs, but complete governing-obligation closure and receipt completeness are not established by this interrupted audit. Missing genuine Native11 delivery independently prevents admission.

newFindings.title: Do not invoke production keyboardCondition during passive eligibility inspection
newFindings.consumerMechanism: navigateSlide's fallback page.evaluate calls priorCondition({ target: active }). The production attachRevealLifecycle wrapper delegates to the previously configured callback, and the actual Reveal keyboard dispatcher invokes its condition again for the real keyboard event. A stateful condition is consequently invoked twice, and the passive invocation receives a fabricated object lacking the pressed key and other KeyboardEvent properties. This violates the explicit N10B-01 no-callback-invocation requirement and can change whether the subsequent real arrow is accepted.
newFindings.repairNeeded: Establish and stage the actual pressed-arrow policy without invoking application callbacks or mutating focus/policy. Where an arbitrary callback cannot be statically/passively classified, preserve that uncertainty instead of executing it during inspection.
newFindings.patchAttribution: navigation.js is one of the eight changed Correction11 helpers in Main's manifest. Exact previous-version line comparison was not performed; this is a current11 obligation failure, not a claim of independently diff-proven introduction.

newFindings.title: Honor the staged keyboard eligibility before sending the arrow
newFindings.consumerMechanism: The helper computes keyboardEligible from keyboard truthiness, input/contenteditable/notes/game/action focus, condition, overlay, paused state and custom bindings, stages it, but unconditionally calls page.keyboard.press(key). For an ineligible focused input this sends an editing key; for a configured arrow callback it executes the overridden command despite already detecting that it is not ordinary navigation. The later target-slide poll is not an eligibility guard.
newFindings.repairNeeded: Prevent a navigation attempt from invoking a known-ineligible or overridden arrow path. Retain complete raw policy evidence and reject unresolved/blocked routing without changing focus or production policy.
newFindings.patchAttribution: Current source violation in a Main-reported changed helper; no previous-version diff was read.

newFindings.title: Assign not-ready detection its actual observation position
newFindings.consumerMechanism: When raw.recorderReady is false, assertAndRecordObservationErrors creates a new Node Error and assigns recorderError.obsOrder + 0.01. An earlier retained recorder occurrence with order 1 followed by capture/state/UI errors with later orders therefore produces recorder, newly fabricated readiness error, then the already observed getter failures. The readiness error was first created during this later consumer call, not immediately after the original recorder failure. The ledger ingests candidates in that synthetic order, so this does not meet S10-C1's actual observation-site chronology/no-invented-order requirement.
newFindings.repairNeeded: Retain the earlier recorder occurrence in its original position, and bind a genuinely newly detected readiness failure to its real detection site after already observed getter failures. Do not manufacture fractional chronology or category-first fallback order.
newFindings.patchAttribution: Current source mechanism in Main-reported changed observation-errors.js; exact prior-version comparison remains unperformed.

additionalSourceObservations.mechanism: Existing recorder envelopes are returned across separate Playwright evaluate calls. The Node ledger deduplicates object references/WeakMap identity only and does not use the document-local occurrence token. Separate deserializations of the same retained browser occurrence therefore are not visibly recognized as one occurrence by this ledger. This is a source-level risk to the explicit forwarding-existing-occurrence-not-duplicate obligation, not an executed browser result.
additionalSourceObservations.requiredFurtherDisposition: Complete governing chronology assessment and distinguish repeated forwarding from new actual getter occurrences before asserting closure.

additionalSourceObservations.mechanism: Browser serializers return null for falsy thrown values, including 0, false and the empty string; the ledger similarly ignores falsy direct input. Nonempty primitive browser failures are enveloped. Complete primitive forwarding is therefore not established. Introduction in11 was not established, and this is not promoted into a diff-proven new finding.

All three genuine caller exposure paths reconcile existing entries only with an explicit valid wrapper phase or metadata; reconcileEntry changes phase only for an explicit nonempty string and mutates the existing serialized object with Object.assign. A phase-less wrapper carrying only metadata therefore does not downgrade an established phase. Canonical original-body disposition and complete receipt verification were interrupted.
